### Insights and directions

**Starting-point insights.** (1) Training margins measure separation from sampled negatives. Their scale dependence motivates rank-based diagnostics. (2) Qualitative feedback suggests excessive broad association and weak current-purpose matching. It motivates controlled recency probes, without establishing individual preferences. (3) The adapter exposes actual model scoring and public histories. Architecture-independent interventions are therefore feasible, while unavailable categories and reviews must remain unused.

**Related-work insights.** (1) [CETRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.03047) separates recency from relative order. This motivates separate interventions, although its LLM findings do not establish SASRec gains. (2) [Petrov et al.](https://research.atspotify.com/2026/10/do-sequential-recommendation-benchmarks-require-higher-order-sequence-modelling) motivate simple history-aware controls. Sequence sensitivity alone does not demonstrate useful contextualization. (3) [Krichene–Rendle](https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.02263) establish inconsistencies in sampled evaluation. Auxiliary diagnostics must therefore remain distinct from the pinned selection metric.

These insights support three directions: controlled temporal dependence, candidate-dependent ranking robustness, and calibration of diagnostics against validation accuracy.

### Framework

| Axis | Existing measurement | Proposed extension | Interpretation limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Representation | Mean embedding cosine | Retain descriptive geometry | Alignment is not necessarily collapse |
| Ranking | Training score margins | Fixed-pool target ranks | Unobserved items are not dislikes |
| History dependence | None | Paired temporal interventions | Dependence is not causal preference |
| Selection | Macro validation HR@10 | Preserve unchanged | Auxiliary gains cannot replace it |

### Candidate ideas

Scores are originality/potential/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

1. **Paired temporal diagnostic adapter — 5/8/3.** Originality: useful controlled combination (+), established perturbations (−). Potential: reusable across architectures (+), observational interpretation remains limited (−). Difficulty: existing scoring hooks suffice (+), padding requires care (−).
2. **Candidate-stress diagnostic panel — 4/7/5.** Originality: combines several candidate regimes (+), components are standard (−). Potential: reveals pool sensitivity (+), benchmark agreement is unknown (−). Difficulty: TF-IDF needs no pretrained weights (+), catalog scoring costs GPU time (−).
3. **Learned recent-history residual scorer — 4/7/6.** Originality: directly tests the feedback hypothesis (+), recency mixtures are familiar (−). Potential: could improve immediate relevance (+), may suppress recurring interests (−). Difficulty: small scoring addition (+), retraining and predictor synchronization cost budget (−).

### Selected idea: paired temporal diagnostic adapter

At 0% progress, establish trustworthy measurements before changing architecture. Sample auxiliary targets exclusively from training histories and construct prefixes strictly before each target. Compare intact prefixes with equal-count recent, older, and random masking; separately shuffle earlier interactions while fixing the latest item. Keep candidate IDs and eligibility fixed within each comparison.

Report target-rank changes, top-10 overlap, sample counts, and category-macro paired intervals. Preserve model mode and all required adapter interfaces. Return measured metrics with explicit definitions; keep unavailable fields empty and uncertainty explicit. Use unchanged host validation HR@10 for model selection. Cache scoring and bound probe batches to conserve the shared GPU budget.

idea.description: Implement a paired temporal diagnostic adapter that measures dependence on recent content and earlier order through the actual trained model, without changing benchmark evaluation.
idea.motivation: The feedback suggests broad associations sometimes outrank specific recent interests, but existing embedding and training-margin probes cannot test that hypothesis. Controlled comparisons provide interpretable evidence before committing search budget to architectural changes.
idea.implementation_notes: Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Call view.model.eval() inside a try/finally block and restore its prior training state. Use torch.inference_mode(). Obtain per-position features through log2feats and candidate scores through predict_score; select the last valid query position according to the architecture's padding convention. Use training-history auxiliary targets only, excluding each target from its prefix. For each user, fix candidate IDs and eligibility using the original prefix across every intervention. Keep masking and deletion/repacking as separate experiments because repacking changes positions. Compute rank changes with a documented deterministic tie rule and top-10 overlap as intersection size divided by ten. Bootstrap users within each dataset, then average the four dataset means with equal weight. Report missing or insufficient samples explicitly. Do not derive compatibility, ownership satisfaction, or simulator traits from interactions. Preserve DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], four-category routing, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, and the existing SASREC_EPOCHS environment default of 200. If subsequent model changes affect inference, update the predictor writer together with training.

originality.positive: Combines matched temporal controls, fixed candidate eligibility, and architecture-aware scoring in the required diagnostic interface.
originality.negative: Perturbation diagnostics and paired ranking comparisons are established techniques.

future_potential.positive: Provides a reusable basis for testing recency mechanisms and checking whether diagnostic changes agree with validation improvements.
future_potential.negative: Perturbed histories may be out of distribution, and diagnostic sensitivity may not predict benchmark gains.

code_difficulty.positive: Requires no retraining, additional datasets, or pretrained weights and reuses existing scoring hooks.
code_difficulty.negative: Correct handling of padding, candidate eligibility, mode restoration, and paired uncertainty requires careful implementation.

related_work.title: CETRec (2025)
contributions: Separates absolute recency from relative interaction order in LLM recommendation, motivating distinct intervention controls.
limitations: Its architectural findings do not establish benefits for SASRec on these Amazon datasets.

related_work.title: Do Sequential Recommendation Benchmarks Require Higher-Order Sequence Modelling?
contributions: Reports strong history-aware pairwise transition controls, motivating tests of whether complex sequence dependence improves accuracy.
limitations: The supplied results concern different datasets and cannot predict performance on the four requested categories.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled ranking evaluation can disagree with full-catalog model comparisons.
limitations: Does not identify which auxiliary diagnostic will predict this benchmark's fixed sampled HR@10.
